    // The signed distance from a point to the triangle with the given vertices:
    // negative inside. Unlike the primitives above this one is NOT centred at the
    // origin — a triangle has no canonical centred form worth the loss of generality.
    // Winding-agnostic: each edge orientation test is compared against the
    // triangle's OWN orientation, so either winding gives the same field. A
    // degenerate (collinear) triangle has zero orientation and therefore no
    // interior, which is why the sign test excludes it rather than calling every
    // point inside — the difference from `Contains(Triangle2D, Point2D)`, which is
    // a closed-set membership test and reports the degenerate case as containment.
    // Exact. (IQ: sdTriangle.)
    DistanceToTriangle(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D): Number {
        var orientation = TwiceSignedArea(a, b, c);
        var inside = orientation != 0.0
            && orientation * TwiceSignedArea(a, b, p) >= 0.0
            && orientation * TwiceSignedArea(b, c, p) >= 0.0
            && orientation * TwiceSignedArea(c, a, p) >= 0.0;
        var unsigned = DistanceToSegment(a, b, p)
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(b, c, p))
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(c, a, p));
        return inside ? unsigned.Negative : unsigned;
    }

    // The signed distance from a point to the quadrilateral with the given vertices
    // in ring order: negative inside. The sign is the even-odd crossing rule rather
    // than an orientation test, so a CONCAVE quad is handled correctly; a
    // self-intersecting one gets the even-odd region, as everywhere else in the
    // library. Exact. Precondition: the ring is simple.
    DistanceToQuad(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D): Number {
        var inside = EdgeCrossesRay(a, b, p)
            .ExclusiveOr(EdgeCrossesRay(b, c, p))
            .ExclusiveOr(EdgeCrossesRay(c, d, p))
            .ExclusiveOr(EdgeCrossesRay(d, a, p));
        var unsigned = DistanceToSegment(a, b, p)
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(b, c, p))
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(c, d, p))
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(d, a, p));
        return inside ? unsigned.Negative : unsigned;
    }

    //==
    // # Sampled signed distance field evaluation
    //
    // Interpolating evaluation of a discretized SDF (`implicit-sdf.types.plato`).
    // The lattice spans Bounds with its endpoints on the boundary, so a node count
    // of n along an axis divides it into n - 1 cells. Positions outside Bounds
    // clamp to the edge cell and the interpolation extrapolates linearly from it.
    // Precondition: at least two nodes along every axis.
    //
    // Fidelity: NOT a bound, whatever the samples hold. Between nodes the
    // interpolant departs from the true distance in BOTH directions, by up to the
    // interpolation error over one cell, so a sphere tracer must shorten its steps
    // by that much rather than trust the value.

    // The continuous lattice coordinate of a position along one axis: 0 at the low
    // bound, count - 1 at the high bound.
    LatticeCoordinate(coordinate: Number, low: Number, high: Number, count: Integer): Number
        => (coordinate - low) / (high - low) * (count - 1).ToNumber;

    // The index of the cell containing a lattice coordinate, clamped so that both
    // the cell and its successor are valid node indices.
    LatticeCellIndex(latticeCoordinate: Number, count: Integer): Integer
        => latticeCoordinate.Floor.ToInteger.Clamp(0, count - 2);

    // The signed distance at a point, bilinearly interpolated between the four
    // surrounding lattice nodes. Not a bound between nodes (see above).
    Eval(self: SampledSdf2D, point: Point2D): Number {
        var u = LatticeCoordinate(point.X, self.Bounds.Min.X, self.Bounds.Max.X, self.Values.ColumnCount);
        var v = LatticeCoordinate(point.Y, self.Bounds.Min.Y, self.Bounds.Max.Y, self.Values.RowCount);
        var column = LatticeCellIndex(u, self.Values.ColumnCount);
        var row = LatticeCellIndex(v, self.Values.RowCount);
        var fu = u - column.ToNumber;
        var fv = v - row.ToNumber;
        var lower = self.Values.At(column, row).Lerp(self.Values.At(column + 1, row), fu);
        var upper = self.Values.At(column, row + 1).Lerp(self.Values.At(column + 1, row + 1), fu);
        return lower.Lerp(upper, fv);
    }

    // The bilinear interpolation within one layer of a spatial lattice: the shared
    // inner step of the trilinear evaluation below, applied to two adjacent layers.
    LayerBilinear(self: SampledSdf3D, column: Integer, row: Integer, layer: Integer, fu: Number, fv: Number): Number {
        var lower = self.Values.At(column, row, layer).Lerp(self.Values.At(column + 1, row, layer), fu);
        var upper = self.Values.At(column, row + 1, layer).Lerp(self.Values.At(column + 1, row + 1, layer), fu);
        return lower.Lerp(upper, fv);
    }

    // The signed distance at a point, trilinearly interpolated between the eight
    // surrounding lattice nodes. Not a bound between nodes (see above).
    Eval(self: SampledSdf3D, point: Point3D): Number {
        var u = LatticeCoordinate(point.X, self.Bounds.Min.X, self.Bounds.Max.X, self.Values.ColumnCount);
        var v = LatticeCoordinate(point.Y, self.Bounds.Min.Y, self.Bounds.Max.Y, self.Values.RowCount);
        var w = LatticeCoordinate(point.Z, self.Bounds.Min.Z, self.Bounds.Max.Z, self.Values.LayerCount);
        var column = LatticeCellIndex(u, self.Values.ColumnCount);
        var row = LatticeCellIndex(v, self.Values.RowCount);
        var layer = LatticeCellIndex(w, self.Values.LayerCount);
        var fu = u - column.ToNumber;
        var fv = v - row.ToNumber;
        var near = self.LayerBilinear(column, row, layer, fu, fv);
        var far = self.LayerBilinear(column, row, layer + 1, fu, fv);
        return near.Lerp(far, w - layer.ToNumber);
    }

    //==
    // # SDF combination tree evaluation
    //
    // Recursive evaluation of a flat CSG tree (`implicit-sdf.types.plato`). Leaves
    // resolve against a caller-supplied primitive list; interior nodes combine two
    // lower-indexed nodes, so the recursion is well founded and terminates on any
    // tree obeying the "nodes only reference lower-indexed nodes" invariant.
    //
    // Fidelity is the leaves' and the combinators': exact leaves under Union stay
    // exact, every other combinator lands on a lower bound, and one leaf that is
    // not a bound makes the whole tree unsafe to march. The per-operator claims
    // are in the distance-operator section above.

    // The combination operator applied to two child distances.
    Apply(combine: SdfCombine, a: Number, b: Number): Number =>
        match (combine) {
            Union => UnionDistance(a, b);
            Intersection => IntersectionDistance(a, b);
            Difference => SubtractDistance(a, b);
            ExclusiveOr => ExclusiveOrDistance(a, b);
            SmoothUnion(radius) => SmoothUnionDistance(a, b, radius);
            SmoothIntersection(radius) => SmoothIntersectionDistance(a, b, radius);
            SmoothDifference(radius) => SmoothDifferenceDistance(a, b, radius);
            ChamferUnion(width) => ChamferUnionDistance(a, b, width);
            ChamferIntersection(width) => ChamferIntersectionDistance(a, b, width);
            ChamferDifference(width) => ChamferDifferenceDistance(a, b, width);
            Blend(weight) => a.Lerp(b, weight.Value);
        };

    // The distance one planar node produces: a leaf samples its primitive, an
    // interior node combines its two children.
    EvalNode(node: SdfNode2D, tree: SdfTree2D, primitives: Array<FunctionSdf2D>, point: Point2D): Number =>
        match (node) {
            Leaf(primitive) => primitives[primitive.Value].Eval(point);
            Interior(combine, left, right) =>
                combine.Apply(
                    tree.EvalNodeAt(left, primitives, point),
                    tree.EvalNodeAt(right, primitives, point));
        };

    // The distance the node at the given index produces.
    EvalNodeAt(tree: SdfTree2D, index: SdfNodeIndex, primitives: Array<FunctionSdf2D>, point: Point2D): Number
        => tree.Nodes[index.Value].EvalNode(tree, primitives, point);

    // The tree's signed distance at a point: the distance its root node produces.
    Eval(tree: SdfTree2D, primitives: Array<FunctionSdf2D>, point: Point2D): Number
        => tree.EvalNodeAt(tree.Root, primitives, point);

    // The distance one spatial node produces.
    EvalNode(node: SdfNode3D, tree: SdfTree3D, primitives: Array<FunctionSdf3D>, point: Point3D): Number =>
        match (node) {
            Leaf(primitive) => primitives[primitive.Value].Eval(point);
            Interior(combine, left, right) =>
                combine.Apply(
                    tree.EvalNodeAt(left, primitives, point),
                    tree.EvalNodeAt(right, primitives, point));
        };
